PERFORMANCE ENHANCEMENT SUBSTANCES 
AND DRUGS (PES/PED): DOPING IN SPORT
The use of performance enhancement substances (PES) is not a 
new phenomenon in sports. As early as 776 bc the Greek Olym-
pians were reported to use substances such as dried figs, mush-
rooms, and strychnine to perform better. Its use is prevalent in 
amateur and professional athletes, receiving even greater atten-
tion with the use by high-profile accomplished athletes such as 
Lance Armstrong, Alex Rodriquez, and Ryan Braun, and dis-
qualification of some professional athletes for failed drug tests, 
and the seizure of companies caught with tainted supplements 
(Pope et al, 2013).
Since 2004, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) has a 
list of banned drugs for athletes who compete and a strategy to 
detect drugs such as anabolic steroids, erythropoietin, human 
growth hormone (HgH), and insulin-like growth factor (IGF-1). 
WADA annually updates their prohibited list of supplements 
suspected of 1) illegally enhancing athletic performance,
